lessons.title: Feel the swing
lessons.dek: Swing is hard to define but easy to hear, once you know what its absence sounds like.
body: Great jazz rhythm isn’t mechanical. Players lean slightly ahead of or behind the pulse, and the tension between the steady beat and where the notes actually land is a big part of what swing is.

In a swinging band, the bassist and drummer lock together. Listen for the walking bass, one note per beat, and the ride cymbal, the shimmering “ding, ding-a ding” the drummer plays to carry the time. When those two agree, everyone else is free to float.

lessons.title: Get inside the sound
lessons.dek: The listener’s job isn’t only to follow the notes. It’s to hear what the musician is doing to them.
body: Two saxophonists can play the same melody and sound like different people. Listen for tone (breathy or bright?), dynamics (does a phrase swell or whisper?), articulation (how notes start and end), phrasing (where the player breathes and pauses), and interplay (who is reacting to whom).
A good solo has shape: it states an idea, develops it, builds tension, and resolves. Try to hear it the way you’d hear someone telling a story at dinner.

lessons.title: Hear the architecture
lessons.dek: Learn two shapes and you can follow most of the classic repertoire.
body: The 12-bar blues: three lines of four bars. The first states, the second answers, the third resolves. One trip through is a chorus.

The 32-bar song form, AABA: eight bars of tune, eight again, an eight-bar bridge that changes the subject, then home. A typical performance states the melody, lets each player improvise over the form, and brings the melody back at the end.

lessons.title: Read the map
lessons.dek: Jazz is a buffet of styles. You don’t need to love them all; you need to recognize them.
body: These recordings run roughly in order, from 1930s swing through bebop, cool, hard bop, fusion, ECM and the 1980s return to tradition.
Styles are easiest to hear by contrast. As each one starts, think back to the one before it: bebop sounds more radical right after swing, and hard bop sounds earthier right after cool.

lessons.title: Listen forward
lessons.dek: Music that seems to have no rules, and musicians making records right now.
body: Avant-garde jazz often comes wrapped in heavy theory. Gioia’s advice is to set that down and respond emotionally first: listen for texture, intensity, and how the players react to each other.
And don’t stop at the dead legends. Jazz is a living music, and a healthy listening life mixes the canon with people making records now.

tracks.title: Jumpin’ at the Woodside
tracks.listen_for: Tap your foot with Walter Page’s bass, then move your attention to Jo Jones’s cymbals. That light, steady push is swing.

art.title: Divan Japonais
art.pairing: A packed Paris café-concert in flat, punchy color; the same nightlife buzz as Basie's band riffing at full swing.

tracks.title: Ko-Ko
tracks.listen_for: The burn: a tempo few bands can hold. Let Bird’s lines blur past and listen to the drums keeping it all upright.

art.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
art.pairing: Bird's tempo is a breaking wave: huge speed, but every claw of foam is exactly where it should be.

tracks.title: ’Round Midnight
tracks.listen_for: A ballad that waits. Paul Chambers and Philly Joe Jones stay quiet, then kick the band into tempo for the solos.

art.title: Nocturne (Nocturne: The Thames at Battersea)
art.pairing: A river dissolving into blue-gray night; Monk's ballad in its quietest hour.

tracks.title: Footprints
tracks.listen_for: Ron Carter repeats one bass figure while Tony Williams keeps reshaping the time around it. Simple, and constantly moving.

art.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake
art.pairing: Figures hurrying across a bridge under slanting rain; it has the same restless, dark forward motion as the tune's minor blues in 6/4.

tracks.title: Body and Soul
tracks.listen_for: A big, robust tenor sound. Hawkins barely states the melody before he is improvising, and every note is full.

art.title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
art.pairing: Deep shadow and burnished gold: Hawkins's big, warm, deliberate tone in paint.

tracks.artist: Count Basie Orchestra with Lester Young
tracks.title: Lester Leaps In
tracks.listen_for: Same instrument as Hawkins, opposite sound: light, airy, relaxed. Could you tell the two apart from two notes?

art.title: Dancers, Pink and Green
art.pairing: Dancers poised and floating in the wings, as light on their feet as Lester's airy, buoyant lines.

tracks.artist: Duke Ellington Orchestra with Ben Webster
tracks.title: All Too Soon
tracks.listen_for: Dynamics as storytelling. Listen to how Webster’s tenor swells and then drops almost to a breath.

art.title: Cremorne Gardens, No. 2
art.pairing: An elegant crowd fading into dusk at a pleasure garden; wistful and over too soon, like Webster's ballad.

tracks.title: West End Blues
tracks.listen_for: The opening cadenza: bends, smears, and a hard attack. Listen to how each note starts and ends, not just which note it is.

art.title: Circus Sideshow (Parade de cirque)
art.pairing: A lone horn player on a gaslit stage in the night; it suits the solo trumpet call that opens Armstrong's record.

tracks.title: Now’s the Time
tracks.listen_for: Try to hum along with Bird. You will fail note for note, and that’s fine; the shape of the phrases will start to sink in.

art.title: The Third-Class Carriage
art.pairing: Ordinary people jostling along in a crowded car, drawn with plain-spoken grit, which fits Bird's street-corner blues riff.

tracks.title: St. Thomas
tracks.listen_for: Rollins takes a small idea and keeps developing it, chorus after chorus. Follow it like someone telling a story.

art.title: Flower Garden and Bungalow, Bermuda
art.pairing: Sun, bright flowers and island air in quick watercolor strokes, as easygoing as Rollins's calypso.

tracks.title: Waltz for Debby (live)
tracks.listen_for: Three equal voices. Listen for who leads and who answers: piano, bass, and drums in conversation.

art.title: Madame Georges Charpentier and Her Children
art.pairing: A soft, tender family scene with children at its heart, for Evans's lilting waltz written for his young niece.

tracks.title: Poinciana (live)
tracks.listen_for: Recorded in Chicago. Listen to how much space Jamal leaves, and how the bass and drums fill it with a groove.

art.title: Oleanders
art.pairing: A flowering branch swaying in a vase; it is relaxed and blooming, with a gentle sway like Jamal's groove (a poinciana is a flowering tree too).

tracks.title: Freddie Freeloader
tracks.listen_for: A 12-bar blues. Count the bars of the opening melody until you feel where each chorus starts again.

art.title: The Spanish Singer
art.pairing: A slouching guitarist playing for himself, unhurried and a little cocky, as loose as this blues.

tracks.title: So What
tracks.listen_for: AABA form. The bridge simply shifts the whole band up a half step. Notice it arrive, and notice how few notes Miles plays.

art.title: Moonlight, Strandgade 30
art.pairing: An almost empty room in cool moonlight; spare and spacious, like the two chords of So What.

tracks.title: Straight, No Chaser
tracks.listen_for: A blues built from one angular phrase. Count the choruses, and enjoy how Monk puts notes in places you don’t expect.

art.title: The Card Players
art.pairing: Blunt, blocky forms set slightly off-kilter, which suits Monk's angular blues with no chaser.

tracks.title: Oleo
tracks.listen_for: A fast AABA tune. Hum the melody quietly under the solos and listen for the moment each bridge arrives.

art.title: Recovering the Stolen Jewel from the Palace of the Dragon King
art.pairing: A daring getaway in swirling motion across three panels, matching the slippery head of a fast tune on rhythm changes.

tracks.title: Ko-Ko
tracks.listen_for: Swing at its most orchestral: Ellington’s sections pass dark, dramatic riffs back and forth.

art.title: Whalers
art.pairing: Dark churning sea and spray, as ominous and powerful as Ellington's minor-key brass.

tracks.title: One O’Clock Jump
tracks.listen_for: The swing band as a riff machine. Listen to the sections trading short figures behind each soloist.

art.title: Study for "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte"
art.pairing: An afternoon built from countless even dabs; it has the steady, gentle four-to-the-bar of Basie's rhythm section.

tracks.title: Misterioso
tracks.listen_for: Bebop as music for listening, not dancing. A spare, walking melody and Monk’s deliberately ‘wrong’ notes.

art.title: Day (Le Jour), from the series Dreams (Songes)
art.pairing: A dark room with one strange window of light, as hushed and enigmatic as Misterioso.

tracks.title: Boplicity
tracks.listen_for: Cool jazz: softer tones and arranged textures. Hear how the horns blend instead of competing.

art.title: Young Woman with a Water Pitcher
art.pairing: Cool blues and soft, layered light with perfect poise, close to Gil Evans's voicings for the nonet.

tracks.title: Take Five
tracks.listen_for: Five beats to the bar instead of four. Count along with the piano vamp and feel how it still swings.

art.title: South Wind, Clear Sky (Red Fuji)
art.pairing: One iconic shape, unhurried and perfectly balanced, as calm and cool as Desmond's 5/4.

tracks.title: Moanin’
tracks.listen_for: Hard bop: bebop with blues and gospel grit. Listen for the call and response between piano and horns.

art.title: Haystacks: Autumn
art.pairing: Heavy earth under a storm-lit sky, rooted and soulful, which fits the gospel call-and-response of Moanin'.

tracks.title: In a Silent Way
tracks.listen_for: The start of fusion. Electric keyboards and guitar, almost no chords moving. Let it wash over you.

art.title: Ville-d'Avray
art.pairing: Silvery trees over still water, floating and pastoral, a scene that waits as patiently as the music.

tracks.title: Birdland
tracks.listen_for: Fusion with a big hook: electric bass, synthesizers, and a melody that builds layer by layer.

art.title: Fireworks at Ryōgoku Bridge
art.pairing: A single burst of light over a night crowd; it is festive and electric, like Zawinul's anthem.

tracks.title: The Köln Concert, Part I
tracks.listen_for: A solo piano improvisation, made up on the spot in one sitting. Notice how long he stays on a single mood.

art.title: Two Men Contemplating the Moon
art.pairing: Two figures lost in a long, reverent gaze, for Jarrett's improvised meditation that slowly unfolds.

tracks.title: Witchi-Tai-To
tracks.listen_for: The ECM sound: spacious, chamber-like, and quiet. Music for people who listen closely.

art.title: The North Cape by Moonlight
art.pairing: A cold northern sea under moonlight, as vast and hymn-like as the ECM sound.

tracks.title: Black Codes (From the Underground)
tracks.listen_for: The neoclassical return to acoustic jazz, played with ferocious precision. Compare its energy with the 1960s Miles quintet.

art.title: The sleep of reason produces monsters (Los Caprichos, plate 43)
art.pairing: Dark, fierce and political, with menace swarming from the shadows; it suits a tense, coded protest piece.

tracks.title: Lonely Woman
tracks.listen_for: Feel it first, analyze later. The rhythm section races while the horns play a slow, aching melody above it.

art.title: Madame X (Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau)
art.pairing: A woman set apart in stark black against bare pale skin, proud and alone, like Ornette's keening melody.

tracks.title: Better Git It in Your Soul
tracks.listen_for: Gospel shouts, hand claps, and shifting tempos. Write down adjectives, not analysis.

art.title: The Harvesters
art.pairing: A whole community working, eating and sprawling in the sun, as earthy and joyfully crowded as Mingus's revival meeting.

tracks.title: A Love Supreme, Pt. I – Acknowledgement
tracks.listen_for: Listen for Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones, the last great bass-and-drums pairing in this guide, and the four-note chant.

art.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
art.pairing: Sky and cypress churning with devotional fervor; Coltrane's prayer in brushstrokes.

tracks.title: Change of the Guard
tracks.listen_for: Right after Coltrane: what carried over, and what is clearly new? Choir, strings, and two drummers.

art.title: Heart of the Andes
art.pairing: A vast panorama on an epic, cinematic scale, matching the size of The Epic.

tracks.title: In These Times
tracks.listen_for: A Chicago drummer and producer. Live playing, edited and layered like a hip-hop record.

art.title: Mäda Primavesi
art.pairing: Layer on layer of looping pattern around a confident figure, like McCraven's stacked, cycling grooves.

tracks.title: Ghost Song
tracks.listen_for: A living singer who moves between standards, folk, and theater. A good place to start following someone new.

art.title: Island of the Dead
art.pairing: A pale figure drifting toward a dark, silent island, a haunting image of longing and loss for Ghost Song.
